Hi J.,

We can do both: an annotated single-PDF export and the per-question evidence set uploaded to Whistic. Proposed plan:

- Create a single annotated PDF (SIG_Responses_v1.pdf) that includes a cover page + question index (question ID, short answer, pointer to evidence file name or Drive link).
- Produce an evidence_map_v1.csv: rows map Whistic question IDs -> file name(s) and internal evidence tag (e.g., "INF-34:Deployment-Logs_2026-07.zip").
- For Whistic uploads, we’ll split screenshots/docs larger than 10 MB into per-section PDFs and add a small index page inside each file with the question ID header.
- We'll add metadata tags in the upload: product=Redwood-API, region=us, release=2026-09.
- Expected ETA: initial upload to Whistic and Drive link by EOD Oct 19, final annotated PDF and manifest by Oct 20.

I’ll coordinate an internal packaging run and share the Drive folder and Whistic job ID when the upload is complete. Does that timeline work for you?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: SIG packaging run — manifest & tagging (action items)

Team — looping you in to execute the packaging run for Acme. External asks above. Please follow the checklist below when assembling the bundle; I included expected filenames and the manifest schema we need for Whistic bulk import.

Checklist (priority order):
1) Export SIG answers from the portal as a CSV with question IDs.
2) Produce a single annotated PDF (SIG_Responses_v1.pdf): cover, question index table (QID | short answer | evidence pointer). Use PDF bookmarks for sections.
3) Evidence files: rename using this convention: "ACME_SIG_<QID>_<shorttag>_v1.pdf" (e.g., ACME_SIG_5_AuthFlow_v1.pdf). Keep filenames < 100 chars.
4) For large evidence (screenshots, logs), create per-section PDFs with embedded index page that repeats the QID at the top. This helps Whistic's reviewer UI.
5) Create evidence_map_v1.csv with columns: question_id, filename, md5_checksum, evidence_type (doc/screenshot/log), notes, drive_link. Compute checksums and include them.
6) Add metadata tags in Whistic upload: {product, region, doc_version, uploader}. We will supply values: Redwood-API, us, v1, marissa_cole.
7) For OneTrust/Whistic: use the portal's "bulk upload" when available; if not, do per-question attach with the mapping CSV. Whistic job name: REDWOOD_ACME_SIG_20261019.
8) Redaction: for SOC2 PDFs that include client names, produce a redacted copy and mark redaction in evidence_map_v1.csv.
9) Drive folder: create folder "ACME_SIG_Package_20261019" and upload all files with a top-level manifest.json (we'll also place a human-readable manifest CSV).
10) Final step: send a one-line confirmation to procurement with Drive link, Whistic job id, and the annotated PDF attached.

Notes / gotchas:
- Whistic has a ~50 MB single-file soft limit; chunk large logs.
- Use consistent QID mapping; mismatches cause delays.
- If a question maps to multiple evidence files, list them in evidence_map_v1.csv separated by semicolons.
- For compliance reviewers, include a "how to reproduce" short note when uploading logs/numeric data.

Action owners:
- Rishi: generate evidence_map_v1.csv, compute checksums, and produce per-QID filenames.
- Diego: create the annotated PDF export (bookmarks + index) and split large docs as needed.

Rishi/Diego — please confirm ETA. I’ll take care of the Whistic job submission and the cover email to Acme.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment stubs: evidence_map_v1.csv, screenshots_tokenization.png
